title.narrative: Council for Soc.Sci Research in Africa, CODESRIA
Rådet f samhvetenskapl forskning i Afrika CODESRIA

description.narrative: Council for the Development of Social Science Research in Africa (CODESRIA) är en pan-afrikansk samhällsvetenskaplig forskningsorganisation med målsättning att stödja och främja forskning och kunskapsproduktion i Afrika. Dessutom stödjer man publicering och spridning av forskningsresultat. Sida ger "core support"(basstöd)till organisationen.

The Council for the Development of Social Sxcience Research in Africa (CODESRIA) is a pan-African social science research organization. CODESRIA supports research and knowledge production in Africa. Besides, the organisation is involved in spreading research and publications on Africa. Sida gives core support to CODESRIA.

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2016Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: The year 2016 was a year of transitions. A new Strategic Plan was approved and new kinds of programmes and, in part, new modes of intervention, using new research vehicles was introduced. The year 2016 was a also a year when recommendations from the three internal reviews started to be implemented. The reforms aim to make CODESRIA stronger and more efficient. At the Secretariat in Dakar the heads of Research, and Training, the Director of Publications, and the Director of the Administration and Finance Department all changed.
Six major international conferences were held in the course of the year 2016: i) a conference on open access after which a Dakar Declaration on Open Access in the South was adopted; ii) a conference to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the Kampala Declaration on Intellectual Freedom and Social Responsibility; iii) a colloquium to celebrate the life and work of Thandika Mkandawire, former executive secretary and renown global scholar; the theme chosen for the celebration: "Thinking African: Epistemological issues", was in itself an illustration of the significance of Makandawire's contribution to the advancement of African scholarship, and to CODESRIA's work; iv) a conference on security regimes in Africa; v) the edition of the annual Gender Symposium held in Cairo, on the back of which a celebration of the life and work of Helmi Sharawy, founding director of the Arab and African Research Centre in Cairo, was also organised; and vi) a conference on (re)making African bodies. The conferences were all very well attended and they were great platforms for debate, and for engaging a broad range of audiences based on CODESRIA's research.
CODESRIA also co-hosted the first edition of the Thought Workshops that brought about thirty well-known African writers, philosophers, and other great intellectuals to Dakar and Saint-Louis in October. A by-product of that event was a long interview CODESRIA gave to the leading and perhaps the most prestigious French newspapers Le Monde.
Many more activities took place in 2016 and the year was a busy year for CODESRIA.
